<cite ref="Sanhedrin 21b:23">Snh. 21ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Megillah 8b">Meg. 8ᵇ</cite> <he>כ׳ עברי</he>(<he>ת</he>), v. <cite ref="L00416"><he>לִיבּוֹנָאָה</he></cite>. [<cite ref="Megillah 8b:22">Ib.</cite> <he>עד שיכתבנו בכתב אשורית</he>, strike out <he>בכתב</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l., a.
<cite ref="Megillah 9a:11">Meg. 9ᵃ</cite>.]—<he>תורה שֶׁבִּכְּ׳</he> written Law, opp. <he>שבעל פה</he>.
<cite ref="Megillah 18b:17">Meg. 18ᵇ</cite> <he>שלא מן הכ׳</he> without a written copy, from memory.—

Pes. 21ᵇ, a. e. דברים כִּכְתָבָן וכ׳ וכ׳ construe the Biblical words as they are written (Deut. XIV, 21) , to the resident stranger give it as a present, to the foreigner sell it.—כְּתַב יד signature.
<cite ref="Mishnah Ketubot 2:3">Keth. II, 3</cite> sq.; a. fr.—
<cite ref="Tosefta Bava Kamma 7:4">Tosef. B. Kam. VII, 4</cite> <he>כ׳ היכר יד שלו</he>.—

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 48:15">Gen. R. s. 48</cite> <he>בכל מקום … הכ׳ רבה על הנקודה אתה דורש את הכ׳ וכ׳</he> wherever you find in the Biblical text the plain writing, i.e. the number of undotted letters in a word, prevailing over the number of the dotted, you must interpret the undotted (ignoring the dotted); where the dotted prevail, you must interpret the dotted, e.g. <he>א̇לי̇ו̇</he> (<cite ref="Genesis 18:9">Gen. XVIII, 9</cite>) read <cite ref="A01183"><he>אַיּוֹ</he></cite>, where is he (Abraham)?; <cite ref="Genesis 18:9">ib.</cite> s. 78; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:5:1">Cant. R. to VII, 5</cite>.—Tosef. Meg. IV (III), 41 (ref. to <cite ref="II Kings 10:27">II Kings X, 27</cite> <he>מחראות</he>) <he>קורין אותו ככְתָבוֹ</he> we read it as it is written (not as emended in the K’ri); a. fr.—Pl. <he>כְּתָבִים</he>, <he>כְּתָבִין</he>. Tanḥ. Masé 1; <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 23:1">Num. R. s. 23</cite>, beg. <he>כ׳ רעים מן המלכות</he> government papers containing orders of hard measures against the Jews. Esth. R. introd. <he>כְּתָבָיו של מלך</he> royal decrees.
<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 20:15">Ex. R. s. 20</cite> <he>עד שילמוד בני כ׳</he> (some ed. <he>כתובין</he>) until my son shall have studied documents; a. e.
